title: The formation law is not fixed: one rule, many laws
plain: The axiom says a site's odds depend on its neighbours. But neighbours form at different times, so which ones count as already there depends on the order sites form, whether neighbours form together, and how unrecorded sites are treated. Each choice gives a different law from the same rule, and the all-at-once (static) law is none of them once a loop exists. The axioms do not pick the order.

title: No rule for where, when and how fast records form
plain: The axioms say records form, not at which site, at what rate, or in what numbers. Written as a mathematical birth process, the allowed rules form a whole family (six free rates for a cube-symmetric one), and nothing picks one. What a sealed box freezes into, and whether that is one state or exponentially many, is decided by the rule you supply, not by the axioms.

title: Records cannot be born by a unitary wave with Born count statistics
plain: Suppose the quantum wave evolves reversibly and the number of records follows the wave's odds. Then a count that never falls never rises, because a reversible rule that creates also destroys. Records could move but not appear. The owner's picture, where the count rises until the box freezes, therefore needs something outside this: a non-reversible step, count odds that are not the wave's, or records that can also die.

title: A sharp one-site birth costs the energy of its bonds, which heat budgets rule out
plain: If a record is a sharp lock of one site, it cuts that site's bonds. The energy is about 2 to 3.7 bond energies for Heisenberg qubits, or 2.4 hop energies for the walker sea. With the lattice tied to the speed of light, that is gigajoules per record at the Planck scale, and at 1e-19 m Earth's heat allows only about 2e-5 births per kg per second. Sharp births look unphysical at every spacing.

title: Redundant readability of a record (local observability) is not derived
plain: The axioms make records permanent and readable only through records. They do not make a record readable by many independent observers, the 'copies everywhere' property that makes a fact objective. This has been an open gate since June. Tests on the lattice's own rules failed: a single site's bit scrambles into its surroundings instead of being copied.

title: The arrow of time needs a low-record past
plain: Records give the arrow its direction, away from the state with fewest records. But the framework does not supply that starting state, and its equations run equally well backwards. Start from a high-record state and the arrow reverses. 'Begin with few records' is an extra input, the same as physics' past hypothesis. Closed reversible rules cannot prepare a blank starting register either.

title: Records alone cannot give quantum correlations; a wave with nonlocal odds is a second ingredient
plain: If records form locally and causally from records alone, their correlations cannot exceed the classical bound (CHSH 2), while quantum mechanics reaches 2.83. A wave over the records reproduces the quantum correlations, but then the odds for a record's next move depend on distant records, and the state is no longer just a configuration of records.

title: The record layer alone is diffusive: waves, inertia and 1/r fields need another layer
plain: Records governed by non-negative odds, like the axiom's distribution, spread out and settle. They do not oscillate. A wave needs signed amplitudes, and inertia or a long-range force needs a rule that is second order in time. So a record can be a source, with mass equal to the record count, but the field it makes has to live in an amplitude layer the axioms do not name.

title: One record per site breaks the exact conservation books and leaves the exchange sign open
plain: Letting a site hold at most one record turns records into an interacting gas. For free walkers that can share a site, energy and momentum are exactly conserved and the gravity route works. With hard-core exclusion the conservation fails at third order and no local fix restores it. The axioms also do not say whether swapping two identical records gives a plus or a minus.

title: Which record is which: identity and the beable are chosen, not derived
plain: In the moving-records picture a record hops between neighbouring sites, but the law that moves them moves unlabelled occupations. Whether 'the record' travels with a particle depends on a naming rule the dynamics does not fix. Following the record that hops, it stays home while the disturbance runs off. Naming by the wave's own bookkeeping makes it travel, but that changes with how the wave is written.

title: Records give an order of events, not a rate: 'time is the creation of records' has no clock
plain: A record history tells you what came before what, and counts records. It does not give a rate. The owner's reading, 'time is the shifting or creation of records', would make local time the local event rate. But events that commute propagate nothing, and a rate needs a physical clock the record order does not supply. A frozen region would be a stopped clock, yet the gravity lane's clocks are assumed to tick.

title: Gauss-law (ice-rule) states are not outputs of directed local formation
plain: The 'photon from a neighbourhood constraint' route needs states where every vertex obeys a balance rule (the ice rule). Tested as the outcome of records forming one after another from local information, no local order, rule or record scheme produces it. The exceptions add a coordinator site or a non-local plan. A balance rule constrains both sides of a neighbourhood at once, while formation reads only the earlier side.

title: Frozen box versus black-hole entropy: no rule and no identified entropy
plain: The owner's picture: a box fills with records until it is frozen, and a frozen box is a black hole. Black-hole entropy grows with the area. For the simplest crowding rules the number of possible frozen states grows with the volume instead, and for other rules it is unknown or unique. Which rule, and which quantity counts as entropy, are not fixed.

title: The record statistical bridge and the composition premise are unadopted
plain: The axioms give odds for which possibility a forming record locks. They give no odds or frequencies for whether and when records form, and no rule for how records combine. An earlier campaign proposed one postulate (formation odds equal normalized weights of the committed action). The owner parked it. So frequency language stays conditional, and the composition premise C-add is carried as a named premise.

title: The motion rule of moving records and the new binding constant
plain: In the owner's picture records hop to neighbouring empty sites 'when the neighbourhood allows'. Two readings of 'allows' give different physics. One has the static law as equilibrium and records that clump. The other has an arrow inside the motion and no clumping. The clumping strength is a new dimensionless number that the axioms' normalized odds cannot see.

title: The rule does not fix one law: no formation order, rate or unit
plain: The axioms say how likely each possibility is at a site once its neighbours are known. They do not say in what order sites get their records. The order matters: different orders give provably different overall laws, and the equilibrium law is none of them. Because the rule looks the same in every direction, no single fixed order can be chosen either. Something must say how records form: a rate, a unit, or a causal order.

title: The axioms contain no dynamics; every dynamics used is a supplied clause
plain: The axioms give odds at a site but no motion: no quantum state, no rule for how unrecorded things change, no clock, no rule that keeps a record once written. Every "dynamics" in this lane is an added sentence, in three separate families, and none is adopted. Records that form only from their neighbours can never reproduce quantum (Bell) correlations (they stay at CHSH 2); a supplied quantum sentence reaches 2.83.

title: The wording of the dynamics depends on what a "record" is, and the simplest reading fails
plain: Which dynamics sentence is right depends on what a record is: a sharp one-site lock, a soft large-scale lock, a marker riding a quantum wave, or something that emerges. Tests so far kill the simplest picture: a sharp lock costs the energy of its bonds, and under a unitary wave a record count that never falls also never rises. No reading is derived from the axioms.

title: No selection principle for the action, the Hamiltonian or the couplings
plain: Nothing in the axioms says which energy function or action governs the lattice, or even that it is nonzero. "No motion at all" fits every constraint proved so far, and the standard candidate actions (Wilson, heat-kernel, Manton) give measurably different answers at lattice scale. Every attempt to pick one has ended with the selection listed as still open. All couplings, stiffnesses and units are inputs.

title: Even given an action, the axioms' odds are not identified with it (the typed interface)
plain: Suppose an action is chosen. The axioms' "odds" are still not automatically what the action calculates. An action gives a state; a state gives probabilities only after you say which question is asked; and the answer must be matched to what the record locks. Small exact examples show each link can fail separately. Owner options for wording this exist; none is adopted.

title: The statistical bridge (Born-type weights) cannot be derived and is parked unadopted
plain: Why should formation odds equal the weights the mathematics suggests (Born-type)? Every derivation door tried is closed at its stated scope: pure additivity cannot force it, no covariant dynamics can pick it, and the last live construction failed its own pre-set test. What is left is adopting it as a postulate. The text exists but is parked; the owner's rule is: identify the action first.

title: The source-to-action and log-det readout bridge lost its footing when Record additivity was removed
plain: The older route from the lattice to an action ran through "the total of a group of records is the sum of the parts". That sentence was removed from the axioms on 2026-08-13, so the log-determinant generating function and what was built on it lost its support. The link from an action to physical sources and readings (charge, mass, gravity) was named open in eight places and remains so.

title: The literal formation law does not propagate; the readings that do add a clause
plain: Read literally, each site gets one record once, with odds that cannot be negative. In the tested versions the laws this produces have the wrong character: irreversible, diffusive, effectively two-dimensional, no travelling waves and no three-dimensional potential. The readings that give waves or long-range order need a sentence the axioms exclude (records re-forming every tick), contradict (records that move), or lack (dynamics for the unrecorded amplitude).

title: Time: no master clock means no propagating field; discrete ticks are exact only for still walkers
plain: If no place has a master clock, a field of clock rates cannot carry a wave: the equations tie each place only to its neighbours and give no travelling mode. Adding a master clock fixes that but gives a speed set by the local rate and no sharp light cone. The lane's gravity-like law is therefore instantaneous (it acts at a distance). With discrete ticks a local clock rule stays exact only for walkers that do not move.

title: Forces as balance-law patterns: the lane's covariant clause cannot move them, and Admissibility is not shown to be such a law
plain: Forces such as light are naturally patterns that obey a balance rule at every site. But any rule built only from neighbouring pairs, including the Heisenberg bond (the only pair rule that treats all qubit directions alike), leaves such a pattern frozen. Moving it needs four-link loops or three-site hops that the axioms do not supply. One qubit also cannot carry a covariant charge or a non-abelian link. So "Admissibility as a balance law" is a hope, not a derivation.

title: One record per site is an interaction that breaks the energy and momentum books; three things cannot all hold
plain: Matter is supposed to source gravity through exact bookkeeping (energy and momentum in equal out). That works for free particles. When particles obey "one record per site" they lose the bookkeeping at leading orders and nothing local restores it; the price of forming a record is not local either. Three things cannot all hold: the chosen gravity field, one-per-site records, and exact equations.

title: No rest energy (mass) is induced; it is supplied
plain: The lane's basic moving particle has no rest mass: the qubit space has no room for a term that would give it one (checked). Mass needs an added staggered term, or binding of two particles; binding works in one dimension but is killed by "one record per site" and is lopsided in three. Rest mass is supplied, not derived.

title: The exchange sign (statistics) is not supplied by records
plain: Do swapped identical records pick up a minus sign (fermions) or not? Both choices satisfy every axiom exactly. They first differ in a fourth-order energy moment, and for the reduced walk their spectra coincide on odd rings. So matter statistics must be supplied from outside.

title: Ordered-phase thresholds are proved far from where they are observed
plain: Does the formation law keep a memory of direction (an ordered phase)? Numerically yes above a modest coupling (about 11). The landed theorem proves it only from about 285,000; the campaign's record quotes 4165, and a refereed, unlanded probe gets 84. The natural proof route was refuted, and the campaign advises stopping. For the sphere version no ordered phase was found.

title: The odds of a forming record are not supplied (the statistical bridge)
plain: The axioms say each forming record draws its content from a probability distribution set by its neighbours, but never say what that distribution is. Every route tried for deriving it from the lattice itself has been closed at the tested scope. The fallback is a new axiom, 'odds equal the action's normalised weights', which the owner parked: it must wait until the framework-level action is identified, and no plain-language sentence for it exists yet.

title: The Born trace form needs menu-independence and menu abundance that the axioms do not give
plain: If a record's odds do not depend on which other outcomes are on offer, and the lattice offers enough different sets of outcomes, the Born rule is forced. Both conditions are extra. The axioms do not supply them, the lattice's own matter law offers too few outcome sets, and the constructed alphabet that offers enough needs further clauses (a scale-reading rule, continuity).

title: Which state the odds are read from: its purity and orientation
plain: Even granting the Born form, the lattice does not say which quantum state a forming record is read from. With the simplest local dynamics the state lines up with the field of the neighbouring records, but how sharply (ground state or thermal), and whether aligned or anti-aligned with the neighbour, is left open. The two signs give opposite correlations between adjacent records.

title: Records alone cannot carry quantum correlations; a wave with non-local odds is a second ingredient
plain: Records that form from neighbouring records alone behave like a local classical machine, so they cannot violate Bell's inequality: CHSH is at most 2, while quantum mechanics reaches 2.83. Reaching it needs a second ingredient, a wave over the not-yet-recorded sites, which the axioms lack. Bell's theorem then forces some non-local element into the odds.

title: What a record is: every reading of "records form" has a price
plain: Something must turn quantum possibility into a permanent fact. A sharp one-site lock costs the energy of the site's bonds, gigajoules per record at the Planck scale. If records never disturb the wave, the wave is a second ingredient with non-local odds. Records that emerge by redundant copying scrambled instead of copying in the tests so far. Soft collapse needs a new length and rate. No reading is free.

title: "Records form" against a unitary wave with Born count statistics
plain: If the quantum wave evolves reversibly and the number of records follows Born statistics, the count cannot go up unless it can also go down. So 'records form from nothing and stay' contradicts a reversible wave. Escapes exist (irreversible collapse, non-Born counts, records as patterns, records that later die), but each is an added premise.

title: Pointer basis, context selection and local observability are not derived
plain: The axioms do not say which quantity a record registers, why it stays stable, or why many observers can read the same value. In the tests so far a bare site does not copy its bit into its surroundings, it scrambles it, and a pointer in a free sea gives a redundancy near 2 (the scrambled value), not 3. Objectivity needs structure the uniform lattice has not supplied.

title: Quantum equilibrium: why records start distributed as |psi|^2
plain: In the version where records ride on a wave, the wave keeps the Born statistics once records have them, but nothing makes records start with them. Out of that state the records could be used to send signals. The framework's realised-state primitive refuses any statement about typical starting states, so the usual fix is closed.

title: The odds are not yet linked to long-run record frequencies
plain: The framework's odds say what a record locks when it forms. Nothing yet shows that counts of records in a long history follow those odds. Counts alone fix no probability law, and repeated records are not forced to be independent. One direct measurement found bulk-record frequencies differing from the weights by 0.05 to 0.12 in probability, stable in lattice size. The theory currently makes no frequency prediction.

title: Quantum kinematics (linear, completely positive, unitary, update) is derived only from supplied premises
plain: Ordinary quantum evolution (linear, reversible, sites combined as a product) is not in the axioms. It has been derived from side conditions such as 'far records cannot signal' and 'pure states stay pure and distinguishable'. Each derivation imports an extra premise, and the step that gives linearity imports the Born weights it is trying to explain.

title: Composition of sites: the joint state space is supplied
plain: Entanglement needs the joint state space of two sites to be the tensor product of their one-site spaces. Locality alone does not force that. The repo obtains it from two supplied admissions or from local tomography. The only alternative tested, a fermion comparator with parity superselection, fails local tomography.

title: No bridge from records or ticks to a clock with a rate
plain: The axioms say records form and stay, and nothing else about time. They do not say how fast, in what order, or how counting events becomes elapsed time. Every lane supplies its own clock. The natural identification, one tick equals one lattice step equals one unit of time, is a naming convention. Different clocks on the same rule give different physics, so the framework cannot yet say what "t" is.

title: The axioms' Z^3 gives a 2D-skewed spacetime or an excluded 3+1
plain: Records sit once on a 3D grid. If that grid is itself space plus time, only two dimensions are space, and the law comes out one-way and lopsided. To get three space dimensions plus time you must let records form again at every tick, which the axioms exclude, or add motion and waves from outside. The good results (long memory, an inverse-distance kernel) live on the excluded version.

title: A propagation cone does not come from records, odds or one-qubit ticks
plain: A light cone needs signals that travel at a finite speed. Odds-based rules (non-negative weights) can only spread out or slide rigidly; they cannot carry undamped waves. Simple one-qubit-per-site quantum ticks are either frozen or move at the top speed with no mass-like curvature. "Nearest neighbour" bounds how far a change could reach only once someone supplies an update rule.

title: Exactly one time (d_t <= 1) is a declared premise; the derivation routes tried are closed
plain: Nothing in the axioms says there is one clock rather than two independent ones. Two commuting clocks fit the axioms. Routes to exclude them either assume the answer, or cannot tell which lattice axis is time, because swapping time with a space axis is an exact symmetry of the staggered hop operator. The result is stated only conditional on a declared premise, B-AXIS.

title: An odd number of time dimensions rests on borrowed anomaly physics
plain: One argument says the number of time dimensions must be odd: a handed (chiral) particle needs an even total number of dimensions, and space is three. But it also assumes the standard anomaly rule, the Standard Model's charges and right-handed partners, none derived here. It yields 1, 3, 5, ..., not 1.

title: One speed for every field is a registered primitive, not a derivation
plain: Space and time could be stretched differently on the lattice, so different fields could travel at different speeds. The framework fixes this by adopting, as an approved building block, that one tick equals one edge in form. Every attempt to derive that from the other axioms is circular or fails. The gravity member is not covered by the block, and on the campaign's continuous-time surface its speed is a free number.

title: One cone is not protected under interactions on the campaign's own time
plain: Even if two fields start at the same speed, interactions shift each one's speed by a different amount, and the shift does not vanish as the lattice is refined. Experiments limit such differences to about one part in 10^15 or better (an external figure quoted in the probe note). A symmetry can prevent it, but the symmetry that works is not the one the campaign's dynamics uses.

title: The Euclidean tick that protects the cone is not the real-time step of the dynamics
plain: The symmetry that protects the cone is a statement about a Euclidean lattice with four equal directions. The framework's dynamics runs in real time. The continuation between the two is proved only for small free systems, and at finite spacing they give different energies. Choosing one changes a headline number (the hierarchy exponent, 16 versus 8), and the tick that keeps a cone cannot carry a one-handed particle.

title: "Time is the creation of records" has no bridge to a clock and clashes with a unitary wave
plain: The owner's picture is that time is records being created or shifted. But if records ride on a unitary quantum wave with Born statistics, the record count cannot rise: records cannot form from nothing. And if a local clock rate is set by record events, Einstein's negative scalar mode either stays or an extra scalar graviton appears; closing it needs an indefinite kinetic form.

title: The arrow of time needs a low-record start
plain: Record formation gives time its direction: away from a start with few records. Why the world began with few records is not derived. The one reduction achieved holds only if records form a single chain, and it leaves the thermodynamic question (why so little entropy) untouched.

title: Three space dimensions are an axiom, not an output
plain: Why space has three dimensions is answered by the first axiom, not derived. The repository's attempt to select three from physics (attraction, stable orbits) works only among a short list of dimensions (1 to 5) and leans on imported physics criteria. Other results (the photon question, the generation count) lean on the number three.

title: The exchange sign: nothing forces fermions over hard-core bosons
plain: The axioms make each site a two-state qubit and allow one record per site. That fits fermions, and equally well "hard-core bosons": identical at one site, but different when two are swapped in two or three dimensions. Every route tried to force the fermion sign has failed. The one theorem that gets it assumes a fermionic (Grassmann) measure at the start.

title: Local fermions on one qubit per site: the string / extra-qubit trilemma
plain: With one qubit per site, a fermion hopping between neighbours in 2D or 3D needs a long chain of extra operations across the lattice (a Jordan-Wigner string). Local codes exist, but they put qubits on links, add constraints, and are not selected by the axioms. So "fermionic", "local" and "one qubit per site" have not been shown to hold together.

title: What is the fermion's local space? Mode, spin coin, or half a composite
plain: Different parts of the lane use the one qubit in incompatible ways: as one fermion mode (the June gate), as the two-component spin "coin" of a walker (September campaign, which also needs four states per site once occupation counts), or as half of a two-qubit composite (Kitaev-style networks). The axioms do not say which. The owner's "particles are patterns of records" reading suggests none is the fermion.

title: Spin-1/2: how a rotation acts on the qubit is a choice, not a consequence
plain: The axioms give the lattice cube rotations and give each site a qubit, but do not say how a rotation acts on the qubit. Four inequivalent ways fit. Calling the qubit spin-1/2 in the physical sense (turn by 360 degrees, get a minus sign) is a further choice: a spin-blind action satisfies every constraint and gives identical numbers.

title: The Dirac law itself: kinetic law, one flux bit, holonomy and time are supplied
plain: The axioms give no motion law. A qubit lattice can just as well move qubits by neighbour swaps, an ordinary slow non-relativistic law with one zero of the dispersion, as by the relativistic Dirac law with eight zeros. The Dirac choice is currently made by adding a class of laws, one sign bit (picked by a thermal requirement), a boundary convention and a time direction.

title: A Dirac mass: rest energy has no source in the rules
plain: A massless lattice walker is a supplied model. Giving it a rest energy needs an extra alternating term (a staggered mass) that nothing in the covariant rules produces. Attempts that derive one need a coupling tuned below a threshold, or a supplied time-reversal-odd term, and often give a rest energy of lattice size.

title: Chirality: every free local walker has a mirror twin, and a qubit has no left/right switch
plain: The weak force treats left- and right-handed matter differently. Every simple free lattice walker comes with a mirror twin of opposite handedness: proved for the campaign's walker (4 right + 4 left) and for any strictly local tick. A single qubit has no left/right switch either. Nothing in the framework yet makes matter chiral.

title: Which hand: the orientation bit is not fixed by anything
plain: Even if the framework produced a chiral rule, nothing says which hand nature has. The axioms name only proper rotations and are silent on reflections, so a handed law needs one extra yes/no datum. The arrow of time does not fix it. The owner has parked the question, with the standing default that neither reading is adopted.

title: Doublers: eight (or sixteen) copies, protected by symmetry, with no rule to keep or remove them
plain: A lattice fermion of this kind comes with 8 copies in space (16 if time is also a lattice). The framework declines to remove them (it treats the lattice as physical), so they must be real particles. Nothing says which are which, what would lift them, or why the count matches nature. The walker's own symmetries keep them in exactly degenerate pairs.

title: Species labeling (AC_phi_lambda): which corner is which particle
plain: The three equal-looking corner states (the hw=1 triplet) are exchanged by a lattice rotation. Any rule built from the axioms treats them alike, so nothing names one as electron, another as muon. The labeling can only come from a convention, a rotation-breaking dynamics or measured values, and the framework has none of the last two.

title: Relativity and positivity for the lattice fermion: the standard spin-statistics route is only partly built
plain: The textbook proof that spin-1/2 goes with fermion statistics needs relativity, positive energy and causality. The lattice supplies none of these exactly. The reconstruction that would produce them from the lattice has been built for the free case only, in two of three pieces, with named gaps, and depends on supporting notes that are not ratified.

title: Reflection positivity of the Kahler-Dirac fermion on non-uniform (curved) histories
plain: Fifty-three notes dated 14 August to 5 September tried to show that the staggered fermion stays a proper positive quantum theory when the lattice cells are non-uniform. Every finite test returned a table with no positive-definite pairing, and no general theorem was reached in either direction.

title: The gauge group is not selected from the carrier
plain: The axioms give each site one qubit, so the only symmetry they hand over is that qubit's su(2). The repo builds a six-state block (3 colours x 2 weak states) to reach SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1). On that block the algebra fits the far larger U(6) equally well. Choosing the product subgroup as "the forces" needs a rule the axioms do not contain.

title: The colour carrier (MR_color) is not derived
plain: A bond of two qubits naturally holds a 3-dimensional block plus a 1-dimensional block, and su(3) acts on the 3-block. Nothing yet says quarks live in that block, that readable records are colour-neutral, or that the colour index rides on the links. Three separate bridges are missing, and the July campaign split them into eight named premises.

title: Non-Abelian gauge links have no account in one-qubit-per-site records
plain: A force-carrying link for SU(2) needs at least four states (two qubits), and one for SU(3) at least six (three qubits). When one is built, the readable pattern of which state each site holds cannot even represent a colour-neutral state in the tested model: none of 65,536 patterns satisfies the non-Abelian Gauss law. Readable content sees colour only through singlets.

title: The gauge action and its normalization (g_bare = 1, beta = 6) are supplied
plain: The axioms say they are not a dynamics axiom, and list "g_bare = 1 convention handling" as an open gate. The repo sets the strong coupling to exactly 1 (beta = 6) by two conditional identifications. One matches the Wilson action's coefficient to a target. The other says a "slot" fixed by rigidity is the coupling. The action's form is also assumed.

title: The SU(2) and U(1) couplings come from a counting ansatz that does not fit SU(3)
plain: For the strong force the repo sets g = 1. For the weak and hypercharge forces it uses g^2 = 1/4 and 1/5, taken from counting generators of the Clifford algebra. Nothing derives that counting rule, and it is not applied to SU(3). An older route instead used one unified coupling at the Planck scale. The two routes disagree on the weak coupling's starting value by a factor of 4.6.

title:
The plaquette value

(beta = 6) = 0.5934 is admitted, not derived
plain: Everything in the strong-coupling chain rests on one number, the average plaquette at beta = 6. Monte Carlo gives it to about 0.06%. The repo has no proof or certified enclosure. The rigorous routes it looked at fail or cost too much.

title: The bridge from the Planck lattice to the physical strong coupling is missing
plain: The lattice coupling is set at the lattice scale. The repo reads it as the strong coupling at 246 GeV, then runs it to M_Z with standard QCD. Run instead from the lattice scale, an ordinary coupling of this size hits infinity far above 246 GeV. A beta = 6 lattice with spacing at the Planck scale would confine near 10^18 GeV, not 0.2 GeV. The 0.1182 match depends on two declared choices.

title: Confinement and the mass gap of the physical SU(3) theory are not derived
plain: The repo's confinement statement is "this is standard Yang-Mills at beta = 6", taken from the lattice literature. What is actually proved is narrower: a gap for one reduced operator, gap positivity on a small compact box, and toy one-plaquette checks. There is no proof of an area law or infinite-volume gap for the physical 3+1D environment.

title: The photon's light-speed dispersion in the qubit-link model is not established
plain: With an ice rule and square-loop flips on link qubits, the evidence says a wave exists that costs almost nothing at long wavelength. Whether its energy grows in step with wavenumber, like light, or with its square, is undecided. The methods in use give only upper limits on that energy, never a lower limit, so a slow mode with small weight cannot be ruled out.

title: The Maxwell dynamics class is supplied, including energy conservation and the time rule
plain: Grant the ice rule. The photon's equations of motion (electric and magnetic fields updating by curl equations, energy conserved, time continuous) are still chosen. Within that choice Maxwell's equations are the unique answer, with one free speed. The choice itself is not derived, and the repo lists three competing ways to discretise time.

title: The photon and matter need one light cone, and nothing forces it
plain: For relativity the photon and the fermions must travel at the same top speed. The approved primitive says the time tick is one lattice edge for matter, but it does not say this for the photon's field. In a tested toy (a walker plus a scalar with a Yukawa coupling) the two speeds drift apart by 0.026 g^2, and the gap does not shrink as the lattice is refined.

title: The link-and-role pattern breaks the axioms' one-qubit-everywhere covariance, and nearest-neighbour formation cannot build it
plain: The photon model puts qubits only on sites with exactly one odd coordinate and uses the rest as bookkeeping. The axioms have a qubit at every site and full cubic symmetry. A nearest-neighbour formation rule cannot make sites obey a balance rule around a neighbour: the chance of a completed pattern is at most 5/16 for the ice rule when formation order is arbitrary and the rule is unsoldered.

title: A field flip conflicts with permanent records unless records move with a fixed identity
plain: In the photon model a flip changes what a link holds, but the Record axiom says records are permanent. Read as records moving round a square, it needs a rule for which record is which. The rule is undefined so far, and different choices give different answers.

title: Electric charge and the strength of electromagnetism are not derived
plain: The strength of electromagnetism and the size of the unit charge are free. In the tested models the charged particle either cannot carry a charge that respects full cubic symmetry, or its coupling washes out the field's stiffness. A finite-size comparator estimate of the pure-ring model's own coupling is about 0.3, roughly 40 times the observed 1/137.

title: The chiral weak SU(2) and anomaly-complete hypercharge are added by premises
plain: The weak force acts only on left-handed particles. Here the su(2) comes from the same Clifford algebra as spin, and nothing makes it a left-handed gauge field. The right-handed partners and the anomaly-free hypercharge come from extra premises. The hypercharge pattern (+1/3, -1) is a left-handed eigenvalue pattern whose overall scale is set by hand.

title: A controlled multiscale flow for gauge fields plus staggered matter exists only in a heavy-mass, zero-coupling corner
plain: The repo's most serious attempt to connect the lattice scale to physical scales runs the gauge field and the staggered fermions together through successive coarse-graining steps. It closes only in a corner (extremely heavy fermions, beta = 0). Six named obstacles remain, each independent of the others, so no controlled flow exists for the physical regime.

title: The Higgs doublet is supplied, not derived
plain: The axioms give sites, a two-state system per site, a neighbour rule and permanent records. Nothing in them is a field that carries weak charge. The lattice object the lane uses as its Higgs source carries no weak charge at all, and a short proof shows it cannot be turned into a charged pair. So every electroweak note starts from "assume a doublet", and the breaking potential and couplings are copied from the Standard Model.

title: Nothing on the lattice action makes the electroweak symmetry break
plain: The lattice's own energy curve for the Higgs candidate only slopes downward; it has no valley where the field could settle. Adding the usual attraction term and asking whether a valley appears gives a clear answer at leading order: the lattice sits at 87% of the coupling needed, so nothing condenses. The notes say the breaking must come from structure not yet derived.

title: Where the sixteen powers of alpha_LM come from (hierarchy magnitude, gate B4 / DELTA0)
plain: The weak-scale formula multiplies the Planck scale by sixteen copies of a coupling (about 1/11). The lattice calculation that yields "sixteen" gives sixteen copies of a different number, which shrinks nothing. Swapping one for the other is bookkeeping, not a mechanism. Five ways to make it real were tried and failed; three remain, one of them untried.

title: Why the exponent is 16 (Euclidean fourth direction and regulator choice, gate B3b / P2)
plain: The "sixteen" exists only if time is treated as a fourth space-like lattice direction, a Euclidean device. With real-time evolution (the lane's own single-clock theorem), the count is eight and the formula lands near 5e10 GeV, not 246. Other equally standard lattice fermions have one, two or four copies. The notes call sixteen imposed by the regulator choice, not derived.

title: Which quantity is "v" (electroweak-scale readout, endpoint L_t = 4, gate B5)
plain: Even if 246.28 GeV comes out, it must be shown to be the size of the Higgs condensate. The formula includes a factor 0.967 that compares a four-step time circle with a two-step one. Nothing selects four steps as physical; an unbounded time circle gives 0.9647 and moves the answer by 0.26%, ten times the claimed 0.026% agreement.

title: Numbers the hierarchy formula inherits (plaquette, bare coupling, Planck ruler)
plain: The formula's answer rests on three inputs settled elsewhere: a Monte-Carlo plaquette value, a convention setting the bare gauge coupling to 1, and the Planck mass as ruler. A 1% error in the plaquette moves the weak scale 4%; 1% in the coupling moves it 17%. The quoted 0.026% agreement is smaller than the 0.4% Monte-Carlo error the repo itself quotes.

title: No controlled transport across the seventeen decades
plain: The top-quark and Higgs numbers come from running Standard Model equations from the Planck scale to the weak scale as if nothing lay between. The lane's own weak-scale formula says sixteen lattice copies switch off along the way, and its own one-step calculation breaks down (the coupling blows up). The running used is a stand-in with unknown error.

title: Top Yukawa, from the exact ratio 1/sqrt(6) to a physical y_t
plain: The lane proves an exact number, 1/sqrt(6), for a weak-charge-blind scalar's coupling to quarks. To get the top mass it must show that scalar is the Higgs, carry the value from Planck to weak scale, and correct lattice-to-continuum differences. That last correction was recomputed in June 2026: about +50% and uncontrolled, not -3%. The top mass is "ballpark", 114 to 197 GeV.

title: The colour-weight selector (kappa_Y, kappa_EW): sqrt(8/9) and the electroweak couplings
plain: A colour-counting choice, whether to keep or drop one of nine colour combinations in a readout, multiplies the top Yukawa by 0.943 and the weak couplings by 1.06. All the framework's good numbers use one choice. The notes prove the axioms do not pick it, and a lattice simulation cannot decide it either.

title: The Higgs mass is the Standard Model run from an admitted boundary
plain: Lattice-native calculations give a Higgs mass of 140 or 152 GeV, 12% and 21% too high. The value 125.1 GeV appears only when Standard Model equations, with imported multi-loop coefficients, are run from a Planck-scale condition "quartic coupling = 0" that the notes admit is not derived. It depends strongly on the top coupling: 1% there moves the Higgs mass 3.4 GeV.

title: The other Yukawa couplings are free
plain: Only the top quark has a candidate origin for its coupling. Gauge invariance allows arbitrary 3x3 coupling matrices, and the trick that seems to fix the top makes the bottom quark 35 times too heavy if applied to it. Two absolute mass scales stay free, and the electron sits 5.5 decades below the weak scale with only a loose numerical pattern.

title: The headline matches carry undisclosed trial factors
plain: Each headline hit (weak scale to 0.03%, top about 172.6, Higgs 125.1) passes through discrete choices made with the answer in view: the exponent, a time-circle length, a colour weight. No note counts how many alternatives were tried. My own small count says a 0.5% hit is not rare. This is a caution on the evidence, not a stuck point.

title: The Koide balance r=1/2: count the paired mode once or twice
plain: The three lepton masses obey Koide's rule only if one paired part of the mass matrix is counted once. Counted twice the rule becomes Q=1, which makes two of the three leptons massless. The lattice gives both readings equal standing and every natural mechanism tried lands on 'twice' or is blind. Nothing derived picks 'once'; what is left is an extra premise.
same_as: gravity-source / statistical-bridge lane (reflection pairing, formation weight)

title: The Brannen phase delta=2/9: from an exact fraction to an angle in radians
plain: The phase that splits the electron from the muon comes out of the lattice as the exact fraction 2/9, a counting density at a cube corner. The measured value is 0.2222 in radians, within 1 sigma of 2/9. No result shows that this fraction is the angle in radians rather than a fraction of a turn or half-turn. Every angle the lattice gives natively is a rational multiple of pi, never a bare 2/9.

title: Carrier and species bridge: the mass matrix, the square-root rule and the labels are supplied
plain: The masses come from a 3x3 matrix on the three cube-corner states. That matrix is supplied, not derived: the free lattice has no mixing between corners, the lattice cannot say which corner or mixture is the electron, muon or tau, and nothing derives why a mass is the square of a matrix eigenvalue. So 'this matrix describes the charged leptons' is an identification made by hand.

title: The absolute lepton scale (a^2, equivalently y_tau) is a free number with two unexplained numerical matches
plain: Even with the right shape, the overall size of the lepton masses is a free number. Two coincidences exist: one ties it to the W mass divided by 256 to 0.03%; the other gives the tau mass from the electroweak scale and couplings to 0.02%. Neither is derived. The exponent 4 in 256 is unexplained, and the Ward-identity route that worked for the top quark is closed for leptons.
same_as: top-Yukawa lane (contrast: Ward boundary works there)
electroweak hierarchy lane (supplies v and alpha_LM)

title: Symmetry breaking S3 to C3 and the handedness choice
plain: If the lattice's full axis-permutation symmetry were exact, the three leptons could have only two different masses. Three distinct masses need that symmetry cut down to cyclic rotations, and the cut has been traced to one yes/no handedness choice. The same choice fixes which sign of the phase is physical. No derivation forces that handedness; the owner has parked the question.
same_as: gravity-sign orientation datum (reading, branch titles only)

title: Why the leptons sit at r=1/2 and the quarks do not (sector spread)
plain: The balance number is 1/2 for charged leptons but about 0.62 for down-type and 0.83 for up-type quarks (at a common scale). Any single rule that gives leptons 1/2 gives quarks 1/2 too unless something distinguishes the sectors. The tested candidates (colour, gauge holonomy, entropy, running, a fixed point) either cannot separate the sectors or put them in the wrong order. The value per sector is a free input.

title: Which mass scheme and scale the Koide relation is claimed at (latent)
plain: The measured masses fit Koide to 6 parts in a million only as pole (physical) masses. Converting the same masses to a running scheme at high scale moves Q by about 1.2 parts in a thousand, 200 times bigger. The repository never says at which scale or in which scheme its derived r=1/2 would hold. It is a bookkeeping gap that becomes a test failure the moment r is derived.

title: Cross-sector link: is the charged-lepton counting channel the one that fixes the quark determinant phase?
plain: Strong-CP (why the neutron has no electric dipole moment) is supposed to follow from the quark mass phase being zero. The lane's registered claim is that the same counting channel that fixes the lepton value also fixes that quark phase. That link is not derived, so closing the lepton counting bit would not by itself settle strong-CP.

title: The quarks themselves (content, colour, charges, Higgs, family labels) are supplied, not derived
plain: The four axioms speak of a lattice, a two-state system per site, a local rule and permanent records. They say nothing about quarks, colour, electric charge, a Higgs, or which family is which. Every quark and CKM result starts from a Standard Model table put in by hand, so the lane can only say "if quarks look like this, then...". Until that table is derived, nothing in the lane is a derivation from the axioms.

title: No rule makes the three generations of a quark type different (no species-differentiated Yukawa/Ward law)
plain: The one clean quark result fixes only the top quark's coupling to the Higgs. Nothing says why up, charm, down, strange and bottom couple with such different strengths. The family symmetry allows at most two distinct values, the gauge rules leave the coupling matrices completely free, and applying the top rule to every quark gets the bottom quark's mass wrong by a factor of about 35.

title: The CKM atlas's building blocks are supplied identifications, not derivations (and the six-state block is the wrong space)
plain: The lane's best result writes the mixing numbers as alpha_s/2, 2/3 and 1/6 and matches data to about a percent. But the rules linking the strong coupling and the counts 2 and 3 to family mixing are stated, not derived, and the notes that prove pieces of it cite each other for the inputs. The "six states" are colour-times-isospin states of one family, while mixing is between three families.

title: Where the quark CP phase comes from, and why it is arctan sqrt5
plain: Quark CP violation hangs on one phase. The lane gets 65.9 degrees by saying one state out of six is special ("1 plus 5"). Other equally natural splits, 2+4 and 3+3, give 54.7 and 45 degrees. The count of six and the split are put in by hand. The older route instead solves for complex numbers so as to match data.

title: Down-quark route: the 5/6 exponent, the GST relation and the choice of energy scale
plain: The lane predicts down-type mass ratios from the mixing numbers with two bridge formulas: |V_us|^2 = m_d/m_s and |V_cb| = (m_s/m_b)^(5/6). So these are the mixing predictions restated, not independent. The exponent 5/6 was the only one of nine group-theory candidates within 10% of the comparator, and only when the two masses are quoted at different energies; at one common energy it is 14% off.

title: Up-quark route: the amplitude law, the up/down partition, and a 10x mismatch in m_c/m_t
plain: Each mixing number is the sum of an up-quark and a down-quark part. The lane gives almost all of the 2-3 mixing to the down quarks, which leaves so little for the up sector that the charm-to-top ratio comes out about ten times too small. A free "partition" repairs it, and one amplitude is chosen from a shortlist because it fits. No rule turns that amplitude into a mass.

title: The Route-2 E-center readout (target triple -1, -2, 21/4): about 110 notes, no derivation, and the match may be a box-size artifact
plain: To fix the up-quark amplitude the lane tried to compute three ratios from how a small 3D lattice box responds to a point source. At one box size (15) they come out near -1, -2 and 5.25. At every other size they are wildly different. About 110 notes have tried to derive the third number; all end in "cannot be derived from what we have".

title: The absolute-mass anchor: the top mass is no longer controlled, and there is no second anchor
plain: Ratios among quarks need one absolute mass to become masses. The lane's anchor was the top quark, quoted at 172.57 GeV within 0.07%, from a Planck-scale rule run down to the weak scale. A June 2026 correction found the lattice-to-continuum step was miscounted; that step is uncertain by about 50%, so the top mass is only bracketed at roughly 114-197 GeV. The bottom Yukawa was also set by hand.

title: No native definition of a quark mass, and the lepton 'dial' does not transfer
plain: A quark's mass depends on the energy scale and scheme at which it is quoted, and light quarks are confined, so "the mass of the up quark" needs a definition the theory lacks. The dial that works (partly) for charged leptons, set to a special value, reads about 0.62 for down and 0.83 for up quarks versus 0.5 for leptons, and no rule sources that spread.

title: Two flavour mechanisms that do not meet: the circulant (leptons) and the tensor/Schur atlas (quarks); small CKM vs large PMNS is a supplied contrast
plain: The lepton side uses a three-family cyclic structure. If quarks use the same structure, up and down sectors are diagonalised by the same matrix and there is no mixing at all. So the CKM atlas uses a different mechanism, and nothing says why quarks and leptons use different ones, or why quark mixing is small and neutrino mixing large.

title: Registered obligation: does the quark determinant carrier equal the charged-lepton K/CPT carrier, forcing arg det M_q = 0?
plain: The strong-CP angle needs the overall phase of the quark mass matrix to vanish. The theory can show this only if the quark's determinant readout is the same physical channel as one already studied for charged leptons. That identification is registered as an open derivation obligation. Meanwhile the quark CP fits simply impose that the phase is zero.

title: Leading-order numerics: comparator choice and imported scheme decide how well the atlas 'fits'
plain: The CKM atlas matches the data to about 1%, but it is a leading-order formula with an imported coupling. The comparator for the CP invariant J differs by 7% depending on how it is built, and |V_us| comes out 1.3% high. Without a derived scale and scheme for the coupling, higher-order corrections can be neither computed nor used to score the prediction.

title: Dirac or Majorana — nothing makes a Majorana mass, nothing forbids one
plain: A neutrino could be its own antiparticle if the theory contained one specific extra term. On the current stack that term is exactly zero, so neutrinos come out Dirac by default. Nobody has shown that no admissible extension could switch it on. Until that is decided, the seesaw mechanism, Majorana phases and the neutrinoless-double-beta rate are unavailable, and the answer is left to experiment.

title: Absolute mass scale — the two routes to tiny masses cannot both be reached from the stack
plain: There are two standard ways to make neutrinos very light: give each a very heavy partner (seesaw), or use an unexplained tiny coupling. The stack switches the first off (W1). Using its own coupling directly gives a neutrino mass about 1 GeV, some twenty billion times too big. The repo's one numerical success uses the seesaw, so it sits on a surface the stack calls empty.

title: The one quantitative success stands on posited bridges
plain: The lane hits one measured number, the atmospheric mass gap, within a few percent. Getting there needs choices the axioms do not fix: two "minimal lift" rules placing the heavy partners on a ladder, a rule for splitting them, a coupling formula that includes a measured coupling, and a weak-scale value from another lane. The staircase notes behind it have never been audited. A ladder this coarse lands this close by luck roughly once in 70 to 200 tries.

title: The mass pattern beyond the atmospheric gap is wrong or absent
plain: Apart from the one good number, the benchmark has the wrong shape: one light state and two nearly equal heavy ones. The "solar" gap comes out about 28 times too large, and the total mass (0.10 eV) exceeds a limit the repo itself quotes. The mixing chart cannot help: its mass-like numbers have a ratio ten times off. No law yet fixes neutrino mass ratios.

title: Mixing angles — the stack gives none, and the extension that gives them is set by the data
plain: The theory's own tools give no neutrino mixing. Large mixing appears only after adding an extra piece with three free knobs, and those knobs are set from the measured angles. One proposed rule (three simple equations) sets the knobs so all three angles sit within 1σ of data, but two of its equations are unproved. So the three angles are inputs, not results.

title: CP phase and octant — the only live prediction rests on a one-bit sheet choice and leans against current data
plain: The lane's sharp forecast is a CP-violation phase near −90° with the atmospheric angle above 45°. The phase's sign is a one-bit choice the theory cannot make: flipping one constant mirrors it exactly. The quoted range was built when data favoured it. The repo's own NuFIT-6.1 comparison puts the current best fit outside the range and the angle below 45°. DUNE and Hyper-K will decide.

title: Three routes to the mixing cannot all be true
plain: The repo tells three different stories about the mixing. The chart fits the measured angles. The records story says the middle neutrino is exactly an equal mix of all three flavours, which pushes θ12 outside the current 3σ range unless another unexplained rotation is added. The mass benchmark instead makes the equal-mix state the lightest. On the same operator they give incompatible answers.

title: The objects the lane computes on are not supplied by the four axioms, and nothing in the lane is audited
plain: Every neutrino result assumes objects the axioms do not contain: chiral fermions, a neutral right-handed neutrino, three generations, Higgs doublets and gauge couplings. The neutrino's neutrality is a labelling convention. The fermion realization is a listed open gate. All 326 neutrino/PMNS rows in the audit ledger are unaudited, and none of 131 lane notes cites the current axiom memo.

title: The theta-free gauge weight (real, positive, Wilson-type) is imported, not derived
plain: The gauge half of the answer works only for a gauge-field weight that is assumed real and positive. Such a weight cannot carry a twist angle. The axioms do not say the weight has that form. A two-plaquette term that does carry the twist passes every symmetry test the lane tried. So the zero comes from the chosen class, not from the axioms.
same_as: gauge action and coupling lane (action-form ambiguity, g_bare = 1)
induced-law kernel lane (POS nonnegative weights, parked)

title: One unsupplied orientation bit sits under both halves of theta-bar
plain: A twist angle needs a sense of handedness: which way is right-handed, and which way records are ordered. The axioms supply rotations but not mirror reflections, so they do not say whether the law can tell left from right. Mirror-asymmetric rules are allowed. The same missing bit sits under the mass half, because flipping handedness is complex conjugation on the qubit algebra. The real weak force is handed, so "the law is mirror-symmetric" cannot simply be assumed.

title: No emergent topological charge Q; the positive route G1-G4 is stalled
plain: To say "the twist angle has a value" you need a whole-number charge counting how the gauge field is wound. On the lattice as given there is nothing to wind: the gauge group at each site is connected, and the only whole-number label found is a three-valued one. Four sub-steps toward a real charge are all open. The lane re-scoped this as not needed for theta-bar = 0. That is true only if W1's premise holds.

title: The mass side is closed only on a supplied surface: real scalar mass, K-real operator, positive orientation
plain: The mass half is closed only if quark masses are plain real numbers on a special hopping operator whose eigenvalues come in plus/minus pairs. The axioms contain no quark masses, Yukawa couplings or Higgs. The July sign-independence proof was marked failed by the audit: at zero mass with a zero mode the determinant vanishes and its phase is undefined.

title: Quark-determinant cross-sector readout (registered open obligation)
plain: Registered open problem: is the object that fixes the charged-lepton counting rule the same physical channel that controls the quark mass determinant, and does that force the quark determinant phase to zero? Nobody has constructed the quark mass carrier or shown the link. What exists is conditional algebra: if the two are the same channel, the phase vanishes.

title: Charged-lepton occupancy grain (registered obligation, owned by the charged-lepton lane; the theta mass side rides on it)
plain: Registered open problem: does the matter action count a particle/antiparticle pair once or twice? Both counts extend the same four-axiom model, so the axioms do not choose. The mass half of strong CP was written to reuse the "once" answer, so it is conditional on it.

title: The determinant-readout interface is entirely supplied, and it is a statement about record readouts, not about the action
plain: The mass-half "phase erasure" is algebra inside a made-up class of readouts: blocks multiply, conjugate outcomes count the same, the readout is additive and reads the determinant. Each was supplied. The additivity clause was deleted from the Record axiom on 2026-08-13, and K/CPT left the axioms on 2026-06-29. Also, the theorem concerns what records can register; strong CP concerns a phase in the dynamics.
same_as: P2 / phase-blindness / log-det readout gate (observable principle)
charged-lepton R-eta readout (same kind of wall, different object)

title: No link between the two halves of theta-bar
plain: Theta-bar is the sum of a gauge part and a mass part, and physics sees only the sum. The lane closes each part with a different, unrelated assumption and has no reason that ties them. The natural tie (one shared real basis for both) was tested and fails because the two operations act on different factors. Without a tie, changing either assumption reopens theta-bar.

title: The axioms supply no dark sector, and the "taste cube" that would host one is an unclosed bridge
plain: The four axioms say nothing about what dark matter is. The dark-matter notes borrow a larger structure, a cube of eight "taste" states meant to carry Standard Model charges, and call two of the eight dark. The bridge from the axioms to that cube is itself on the axiom memo's list of open gates. So the framework has no derived answer yet to "what is dark matter".

title: The notes give the dark state incompatible charges, and offer three mutually exclusive dark candidates
plain: Different dark-matter notes describe different particles. One says the dark particle feels no force but gravity, is Planck-mass, and cannot be tested. Another treats it as a 3.9 TeV particle that annihilates through a gauge-like force, and its mass derivation needs it to carry colour charge. A third calls a right-handed neutrino the "DM candidate", though that particle decays in about 10^-30 seconds. These cannot all hold.

title: The dark mass 16 v was found by scanning against the abundance target, and no mechanism exists
plain: The dark mass, 16 times the electroweak scale (3.94 TeV), was found by searching a list of framework numbers for one that makes the observed baryon asymmetry come out. Every attempt to explain why the mass should be 16 v has failed, been corrected, or stayed a numerical coincidence. So the mass is a fit to the answer, not a prediction.

title: The annihilation force and the coupling in the Sommerfeld factor are chosen, not derived
plain: How much dark matter survives depends on how strongly it annihilates. The notes pick the coupling from a range: 0.03 to 0.05 in one note, about 0.091 to 0.092 in others, and these give different answers. A dark particle that feels no gauge force would not have that coupling at all. The resulting dark-to-ordinary ratio comes out 1.5 to 2% above the measured 5.36.

title: R = R_base x S is a group-theory identity presented as the physical dark-to-baryon density ratio
plain: The number 31/9 is exact arithmetic on group-theory constants. Nothing shows why the real ratio of dark to ordinary matter should equal it. The lane's own earlier note showed that ordinary matter is left over from a matter-antimatter imbalance, not from annihilation freeze-out, so a ratio of annihilation strengths cannot give it. Later notes reuse the number to compute the imbalance.

title: The baryon asymmetry eta is imported, and both derivation routes are blocked
plain: The lane needs the amount of ordinary matter, which comes from the matter-antimatter imbalance eta, and takes it from observation. The neutrino route to eta gives 0.19 of the observed value. Reaching 1.0 needs a neutrino-phase sign that no note can derive, and about thirty notes close the alternative routes. The old electroweak route stalls on undetermined inputs.

title: The thermal, cosmic-history substrate of a relic abundance is imported
plain: A relic abundance is a statement about a hot, expanding early universe cooling past a freeze-out point. The axioms give no time metric, no expansion law, no thermal state and no starting condition. The framework's cosmology inputs (Friedmann law, particle count, today's temperature, freeze-out constant) are imported or conditional, and the repo's current rule is that an unresolved cosmology input supplies no premise.

title: Vacuum energy is about 10^123 too big and no mechanism removes it
plain: Adding up the energy of empty space on the lattice gives about one Planck unit per cell. Observed dark energy is about 10^-123 of that. The lane tried five ways to shrink the sum and none worked. The newest lattice work shows the lattice's empty-space energy is not even constant as the lattice stretches, so it does not act like a cosmological constant.

title: The size of the cosmos (R_Λ/a ≈ 10^61) and H_0 are put in by hand
plain: The lane proves a tidy formula, Λ = 3/R², but the radius R, in lattice units, is not derived. The quoted agreement (a factor 1.44 off) uses the measured Hubble rate. The notes say what is missing is a way to fix R without the observed H_0, and a gravity input (lattice spacing equal to the Planck length) that no one has derived.

title: The 3-sphere behind Λ = λ₁(S³) may be a renaming, and it clashes with the flat space used elsewhere
plain: To get Λ the lane treats space as a 3-sphere of radius R. To get the expansion, matter fractions and baryon asymmetry it assumes space is flat. A sphere of the size that gives the observed Λ would make space visibly curved, which observation rules out. The "identity" also only says a de Sitter universe of radius R has Λ = 3/R², which is geometry, not a derivation.

title: Expansion has no native meaning under the axioms; the Friedmann backdrop is supplied
plain: The lattice is fixed and the axioms have no time metric or gravity. The cosmology stack assumes a uniform, smoothly expanding universe obeying the Friedmann equations with a standard matter and radiation mix. The lane's own open gate lists three of those assumptions as supplied. The newest lattice work gets Friedmann-like equations only after a length-growth law is supplied.

title: The uniform, low-disorder start (past hypothesis, homogeneity, no heat added later) is handed in
plain: Cosmology needs a very special beginning: nearly uniform, low disorder, and no extra heat injected later. The axioms only say a state is a set of records and that the law favours no state. So the special start, and the uniformity of the sky, must be supplied. The lane names this and prices it as an input; nobody has tried the horizon problem.

title: Matter and dark-energy fractions today need cosmic-history numbers the axioms do not supply, and "why now" has no route
plain: Once the cosmic size is fixed, the fractions of matter and dark energy today need one more number about cosmic history. The lane proved the axioms do not supply it and found two ways it could come. One runs through the baryon asymmetry and a coupling; the other, a direct derivation, has no candidate. Nothing explains why matter and dark energy are comparable now.

title: The baryon asymmetry is reached only by choosing a point, and its CP sign has no source
plain: The lane's clean calculation gives a baryon asymmetry about five times too small (0.19 of observed). A more elaborate version reaches exactly the observed value, but only by choosing a point in a family of solutions. What is left is one sign: which way CP violation points. Every selector in the lane is blind to that sign, and a separate no-go says the tested routes cannot source it.

title: The leptogenesis machinery is not in the four axioms
plain: To make a matter excess you need heavy neutrinos, a hot expanding bath, standard-model particle counts and a process that turns lepton number into baryon number. The lane supplies each as a named packet. Its audit-critical upstream steps were flagged as needing new derivations from the axioms, and none exists. Without them the chain is arithmetic on supplied inputs.

title: Inflation and the primordial spectrum are asserted, not derived
plain: The lane "predicts" the spectral tilt by growing a graph and counting random noise. The correction that makes it match slow-roll inflation is written in without derivation, the number of e-folds (60) is put in, and a claim that 10^78 nodes "matches" the 10^183 Planck cells in the universe is off by about 105 orders of magnitude. A growing graph is not in the axioms either.

title: No finite-site graviton with Einstein's spectrum (too slow, or a wobble comes with it)
plain: Einstein's gravity waves have two fingerprints: light speed, and one shape only, a stretch-and-squeeze across the direction of travel. Every way tried to build them from finite, record-like pieces on the fixed grid misses one. Strict local rules make the waves crawl. Loosening the rules makes them light-fast but adds a sideways wobble the double pulsar excludes unless it runs more than twelve times faster. Only continuous numbers at each site have worked.

title: Einstein's wrong-sign conformal mode is needed, and a ground state cannot supply it
plain: Einstein's own theory has one direction, the overall size of space, whose energy runs backwards; his time rule hides it. To remove the wobble from a lattice graviton, the lattice would need that backwards-running direction too. A system in its lowest-energy state cannot have it. Forcing it gives a knife edge, a ghost and a flat gapless band. The same sign problem shows up in every gravity lane.

title: A composite graviton's extra modes have no known gapping mechanism
plain: One way out keeps finite sites and exact rules: build the graviton as a bound state of simpler fields, for example three photon-like fields. It can look light-speed and pure at first, but its unwanted partners then have to be removed by some strong-coupling effect. None is known. The one literature candidate, from Gu and Wen, is called unreliable by its own authors.

title: The two owner-level exits that keep the axioms' finite sites (recorded adjacency; strongly correlated or non-local gravity) have no bounded test
plain: If continuous numbers per site are refused, two choices remain: let the grid's connections themselves be the geometry, or say gravity is a strongly interacting many-body pattern with no simple wave description. For neither is there a test anyone can run. The first also makes the Record axiom circular, because records sit on sites that would then be made of records.

title: Gravity as an equation of state of entanglement does not work on the fixed cubic grid
plain: One way to avoid a graviton field is to get Einstein's equation from how entanglement grows with area. On this grid the entanglement per unit area differs by 16–18 % between cut orientations, so there is no single coefficient, and the derivation needs a metric and boosts the axioms do not supply. I reproduced the orientation difference with my own code.

title: Nonlinear closure of gravity's constraint algebra on the fixed lattice
plain: Einstein's theory hangs together only if its rules keep working when the field is strong, not just for small waves. On a fixed grid that is known to be hard, because the tools that guarantee it fail for lattice brackets. At small amplitude the clock rules close only at one special ratio. Beyond that the walker's clocks close only for uniform lapses. The test that would settle the next order is not yet specified.

title: The geometric carrier (metric, clock rate, lengths, tensor slots) is supplied; there is no Record-to-geometry map
plain: Every working piece of gravity in the repository starts from something the axioms do not contain: a metric with continuous lengths and angles, a tick rate per site, or a tensor field. The step from records to geometry has never been built: no records-to-event-order map, no derived clock rate, no lengths from records. Gravity therefore comes out only relative to a supplied geometry.

title: Einstein's action itself is not derived (direct route blocked; induction needs the metric posit and may not give the Einstein form)
plain: Even given a metric, the repository has not shown that the lattice produces Einstein's gravitational action. The direct route from the determinant of the Dirac operator lacks a step. The induced-gravity route needs the metric to exist as a field, and on a fixed lattice it may not give the Einstein form at all, only mass-like terms and direction-dependent speeds.

title: The curvature member (and so light bending by twice the Newtonian value) is declared, not forced
plain: The clock-only law bends light by half the Einstein value. Getting the full factor needs the lattice also to stretch space near a body, which the clock law does not do: a body at rest sources no lengths. The repository gets the factor 2 by declaring an action whose exponent, linearity in the clock rates, stiffness and sign are chosen rather than derived.

title: The source/action bridge: what sources gravity, and with what absolute strength and unit
plain: Gravity has to know what makes it: energy, a record count, or a compressed density, and with what strength. The axioms list "source/action identification" as an open gate. The lattice lane assumes the source is the walkers' energy when a ledger is kept. Nobody has derived that assumption, and the strength is still free.

title: The magnitude of Newton's constant in lattice units, and a = l_P, is not derived (three unreconciled candidates)
plain: The framework fixes only a ruler: the lattice spacing is set equal to the Planck length by definition of its one reference. Whether its own internal gravity has exactly that strength is called "a separate open gravity derivation". Three routes give three answers: Newton's constant of order the spacing squared over the number of species, exactly 1 under a supplied boundary-count premise, and a free stiffness. None is derived.

title: That gravity attracts (the sign of the coupling) is not derived
plain: Nothing in the repository derives that gravity attracts. Three natural arguments, from spectra, from stability and from the arrow of time, do not force it, and stability actually favours repulsion. Each lane reduces the sign to one supplied choice: an orientation datum, whether records slow the clocks around them, or the sign of the size-of-space kinetic term.

title: Lattice matter has no exact local stress-energy books (momentum, angular momentum) once it interacts or excludes
plain: A graviton can couple consistently, and stay massless, only to matter whose energy and momentum are conserved exactly at each place. Lattice matter conserves energy locally but generally not momentum. Under the one-record-per-site rule or with scattering, the bookkeeping fails at third order or entirely, and angular momentum cannot be kept with momentum on six axes unless records never scatter.

title: Universality of free fall (the equivalence principle) holds only under a list of conditions
plain: Gravity must pull every kind of matter the same way. In the lattice lane that holds only under conditions: the curvature member, first order in the field, a particular momentum definition, and for bound groups an extra "binding clause". Some species fall with minus their weight, and records in a clock gradient settle with a weight but do not drift alike.

title: A fixed regular lattice gives the graviton mass-type terms and destabilising shear energy unless several numbers are tuned
plain: A regular grid has a shape. Couple the walker's vacuum to a constant metric in the natural way and its energy changes when the metric shears the grid, which costs nothing in real gravity. That acts like a graviton mass of the vacuum's size unless several numbers are tuned, and for interacting matter the cancellation returns at the next order. I reproduced the basic numbers.

title: The graviton's speed must equal the matter light speed, and only an added premise protects it
plain: Light and gravity waves must travel at the same speed to about one part in 10¹⁵. In the lattice comparator the speeds of two coupled fields drift apart at second order, by an amount that does not shrink as the grid gets finer. An added rule (a tick counts like a space step) protects them; it is approved for matter but not for the gravity field.

title: No positive physical reconstruction of a lattice gravity action has been found; the reflection-positivity route has only negative finite results and its bridge is parked
plain: The older "gravity mainline" tried to make a lattice gravity action pass a positivity test, so that it defines a real quantum theory with only positive-norm states. In every finite case tried it failed: the reflected-curvature action has wrong-sign spin-2 modes and an extra indefinite channel. The route was called closed, but the landed notes were corrected to claim only their finite fixtures. What remains is a parked owner decision.

title: What gravitates: the member's zero mode tests the zero of energy (vacuum energy)
plain: It is not settled whether gravity sees the vacuum. The walker's filled sea carries about one hop of negative energy per site. If the gravity field sees it, a closed lattice bounces or cannot move at all; if not, the framework has to supply the zero of energy by hand. This is the cosmological-constant problem in the lattice's own terms.

title: Clause C1 (every site's clock ticks at a positive rate) conflicts with the owner's stopped-clock (frozen-box) reading
plain: The source-link lane assumes every site's clock ticks at a positive rate, which rules out a stopped clock. The owner's reading, that a box which can form no more records is frozen and that time is the making of records, needs a rate that can reach zero, as at a horizon. As they stand, the two readings do not fit together.

title: The 1/4 is a count of a supplied cell, not an entropy, and is not tied to gravity (BP)
plain: The framework's "1/4" is a counting fact: 4 of the 16 states of a four-slot cell the notes supply. Black-hole entropy is a different kind of number: entropy per unit of horizon area. Nobody has shown from the axioms that the count is the entropy, or that this cell has anything to do with gravity. The notes call this the bridge premise (BP) and leave it open.

title: The axioms define no entropy; the lane uses five that disagree
plain: The axioms give records: permanent, one per site, readable. They give no state vector, no weighting of outcomes and no entropy. The lane has used five different "entropies": a rank count, a count of frozen record patterns, an outcome-weighted entropy, fermion entanglement, and Wald's Noether charge. They disagree. Until the axioms pick one, "entropy = area over four" has no fixed meaning.

title: Exactly 1/4 from entanglement needs a hand-picked selector, and the natural law has a logarithm
plain: If the entropy is the entanglement of ordinary lattice fermions, the natural answer is one sixth of the boundary times a logarithm of the size, not one quarter. Getting exactly 1/4 needs a hand-picked extra ingredient (a half-filled zone, a two-band edge, a special edge probability), each a tuning knob. A finite-state edge built from algebraic numbers cannot give exactly 1/4 at all.

title: The lane's own numerical test cannot yet tell 1/4 from 1/6; part of the excess is a zero-mode effect
plain: The lane's own numerical test looks close to 1/4 at the sizes tried (0.257 at size 64), but the number is still falling. Fit it one way and it heads to 1/4, another way to 1/6. My rerun shows about half of the excess over 1/6 at size 40 comes from a mixed-state device used to handle degenerate zero-energy states. The proof that would settle the limit does not exist.

title: Newton's constant in lattice units is set by the black-hole match itself, or by a free stiffness
plain: The 1/4 fixes the lattice spacing only if gravity's strength in lattice units is known independently. In the notes it is not: the value "Newton's constant = 1" comes from demanding the black-hole match, so the match cannot then test it. The recent gravity work also has a free stiffness number that plays the same role.

title: No lattice derivation of a horizon; the thermodynamics is standard general relativity on an assumed surface
plain: Black-hole thermodynamics in the notes (Hawking temperature, first law, Bekenstein bound) is standard general relativity on a smooth spacetime that is assumed, not derived from the lattice. Lattice results point the other way: clocks slow but never stop, older strong-field runs find a floor, not a horizon, and the tensor-gravity probes find no clean light-speed graviton. What a black hole is in this framework is unsettled.

title: Hawking radiation has no lattice derivation; the one lattice test failed and was retracted
plain: Hawking radiation appears only as a temperature formula borrowed from smooth spacetime. The one lattice test (a "Hawking analog") gave amplification instead of trapping, and its temperature-versus-gravity sign was wrong; its headline was retracted. A real evaporation model also needs something that traps and then leaks, which permanent records and unitary evolution do not obviously allow. Nobody has built one.

title: The owner's frozen-box reading has no formation rule and the count grows with volume, not area
plain: The owner's picture: a sealed box fills with records until nothing more can form, and a frozen box is a black hole.
